questions.q: A process has $\Delta H = 200Jmol^{- 1}$ and $\Delta S = 40JK^{- 1}mol^{- 1} .$ Out of the values given below choose the minimum temperature above which the process will be spontaneous:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$∆ G = ∆ H - T ∆ S$ ....... (Gibbs Helmholtz Equation)

For a reaction to be spontaneous, $∆ G < 0$

So, $∆ H - T ∆ S < 0$

$∆ H < T ∆ S$

$\dfrac{∆ H}{∆ S} < T$

i.e. Minimum temp. should be $⇒ \dfrac{∆ H}{∆ S} = \dfrac{200}{40} = 5K$

For an adiabatic free expansion of an ideal gas, the gas is kept in an insulated container and then permitted to enlarge in a vacuum. Since there is no external pressure for the gas to enlarge against, the work done by or on the system is zero. Since this process does not involve any exchange of heat transfer or work, heat will not escape and temperature of system will rise.

For diathermic container, heat will escape the container and hence temperature of container will remain same.

questions.q: If three moles of an ideal gas at $300K$ expand isothermally from $30{dm}^{3}$ to $45{dm}^{3}$ against a constant opposing pressure of $80$ kPa, then the amount of heat transferred is __________J.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Given,

${V}_{1} = 30{dm}^{3}{V}_{2} = 45{dm}^{3}P = 80kPa$

Using, first law of thermodynamics,
$\Delta U = Q + W$

$Q$ is the heat given or lost

$\Delta U$ is the change in internal energy

$W$ is the work done

$\Delta U = 0$ : Process is isothermal

$Q = - W$

$W = - {P}_{ext}\Delta V:$ Irreversible

$W = - {P}_{ext} ( {V}_{2} - {V}_{1} )$

$= - 80 \times {10}^{3} ( 45 - 30 ) \times {10}^{- 3}$

$= - 1200J$

Hence, the amount of heat transferred is $1200J$
